test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 03 Sept, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is an example of globalisation in India post-1991?

options.text: Entry of multinational companies like Amazon and Apple

solution:
The correct answer is __**Entry of multinational companies like Amazon and Apple**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Globalisation in India post-1991 was marked by the **liberalisation policies introduced under the New Economic Policy**, allowing foreign direct investment (FDI) and the entry of multinational corporations (MNCs).
 
• Companies like **Amazon, Apple, Google, and Microsoft** entered the Indian market, bringing advanced technologies and global business practices.
 
• This shift allowed Indian consumers to access global brands and products, thereby increasing competition and improving quality standards.
 
• The **Information Technology (IT) and software sector** experienced exponential growth due to globalisation, with companies like Infosys and TCS becoming global players.
 
• Globalisation also facilitated **outsourcing**, where India became a hub for IT services, call centers, and manufacturing for multinational companies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nationalisation of major private banks:**

 
 
• Bank nationalisation refers to the process where private banks were taken over by the government.
 
• In India, major bank nationalisation occurred in 1969 and 1980 to improve financial inclusion and provide banking services to underserved areas.
 
• This measure does not represent globalisation but rather reflects government control and regulation of the banking sector.
 
 
 
• **Licensing requirement for all businesses:**
 
 
• Before the 1991 reforms, India followed a stringent **License Raj system**, where businesses needed multiple licenses and approvals to operate.
 
• The 1991 economic reforms dismantled this system, leading to liberalisation and the removal of excessive licensing requirements.
 
• While this change encouraged private sector growth, it is not directly linked to globalisation but rather to domestic liberalisation.
 
 
 
• **Closure of ports:**
 
 
• Closure of ports is not related to globalisation; instead, globalisation involves increasing trade and connectivity through port operations.
 
• India expanded its port infrastructure post-1991 to boost international trade, such as the development of major ports like Mumbai and Chennai.
